title: Frontend mid scenario accessibility audit
question: You've been asked to run an accessibility audit on an existing product page before launch. What would you actually check, beyond running an automated tool?
idealAnswer:
Automated tools (like axe or Lighthouse) only catch a fraction of real issues, roughly the mechanically checkable ones like missing alt text or contrast ratios, they can't judge whether alt text is actually meaningful or whether a flow makes sense

Test full keyboard navigation manually: can every interactive element be reached and operated with Tab/Shift+Tab/Enter/Space/Arrow keys alone, is focus order logical, and is the currently focused element always visibly indicated

Test with an actual screen reader (VoiceOver, NVDA, or similar) on the key user flows, not just individual elements, to check that headings, landmarks, form labels, and dynamic content announcements make sense as a coherent experience

Check that dynamic UI updates (toasts, validation errors, loading states) are announced to assistive tech, e.g. via aria-live regions, not just visually shown

Check color contrast in context (including on hover/focus/disabled states, not just default state) and confirm no information is conveyed by color alone

Check that modals and dropdowns trap focus appropriately while open and restore focus to a sensible place when closed
